_README: Bone collagen turnover for the bone (cross-sectional) weaning model: the share of a young animal's bone collagen that is newly made each month, at each age. Values are monthly shares; a yearly turnover rate T (as in WARN) converts as 1 - exp(-T/12). In growing animals most new collagen comes from skeletal growth, so the share is high at birth and falls with age. WARN (Tsutaya & Yoneda 2013) estimated these values for human rib bone from tissue-level bone data (included below as 'human', for checking against WARN); no equivalent values are established for livestock. Every livestock table here is a PLACEHOLDER (TBD-LAB): replace it with values from bone growth and remodelling data for the species (e.g. skeletal mass gain with age plus remodelling rate), then set placeholder to false.

tables.label: Human rib collagen (WARN; Tsutaya & Yoneda 2013, Table 1)
tables.source: Tsutaya T, Yoneda M (2013) PLoS ONE 8: e72327, Table 1, 'Collagen (QP)' turnover per year for each year of age 0-10. Converted to a monthly share as 1 - exp(-T/12) and placed at the middle of each year; the first year's value is also used at birth. (The quartic printed as Eq. 6 does not reproduce Table 1 beyond about age 2, probably because its coefficients are rounded, so the table is used.)
